final_narrative:
The nine differentially-abundant metabolites point to a disruption of xenobiotic metabolism. The RaMP enrichment identified **Biological oxidations** as the top pathway (fold 128.5, FDR 0.0, matched by C00097, C01324, C05851, C14853, C20319, C07190, C00928), with strong co-enrichment of **Phase II – Conjugation of compounds** (fold 159.1, FDR 0.0), **Phase I – Functionalization of compounds** (fold 121.9, FDR 1 × 10⁻⁶), **Metabolism** (fold 31.8, FDR 0.0), and **Xenobiotics** (fold 346.4, FDR 2 × 10⁻⁶). All five are Reactome-annotated pathways.

**Key driver compounds.** The benzo[a]pyrene-7,8-dihydrodiol-9,10-oxide (C14853) is directly annotated to Biological oxidations, Phase II – Conjugation of compounds, and the sub-pathway Glutathione conjugation (R-HSA-156590). L-Cysteine (C00097) is matched in both the Biological oxidations and Phase II enrichments; as the glutathione precursor, it anchors the conjugating capacity of the pathway. Coumarin (C05851) is annotated to Phase I – Functionalization of compounds and the sub-pathway Cytochrome P450 – arranged by substrate type (R-HSA-211897). N-hydroxy-4-aminobiphenyl (C20319) appears in both Phase I and Phase II as well as the Xenobiotics pathway; methimazole (C07190) appears in Phase I – Functionalization of compounds.

**Upstream/downstream relationships.** The KEGG reaction graph confirms L-Cysteine (C00097) connects to glutathione (C00051) in two hops via gamma-glutamylcysteine (C00669), supporting the claim that cysteine availability constrains Phase II conjugating capacity.

**Biological significance.** The co-enrichment of Phase I and Phase II pathways indicates that the treatment affects both the oxidative and conjugative arms of xenobiotic metabolism. Elevated benzo[a]pyrene epoxide alongside altered L-cysteine and coumarin is consistent with increased PAH bioactivation, impaired Phase II detoxification, or both. Methimazole and bromide further suggest halogenated compound or thionamide drug metabolism. Together these changes describe a multi-pathway disruption of cellular defence against electrophilic toxicants.

**Limitations.** Fold-enrichment values and Reactome identifiers were taken directly from the enrichment output; the relative ranking of pathways beyond the top-1 position was not independently verified by direct membership queries in all cases. In addition, 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid (C00632) and dihydrobiopterin (C02953) were not matched in the top five enriched pathways and their contribution to the observed signal remains uncharacterised.
